The move came after pilots reported cases of suspected fumes leaking into the cockpit and cabin, causing migraines and other symptoms during flight, according to the report.
The affected aircraft are less than four years old and contain new, more fuel-efficient engines developed by Pratt & Whitney that entered into service with Air Corsica in 2022.
It is not yet clear whether the underlying cause of the reported fumes is specific to Air Corsica’s fleet or reflects a more fundamental flaw with the aircraft or the new engine.
